Repository: astropy/astropy
Base commit: e2a2ca3eab1defc71aedf4cf3982f7d4793faacf
### Issue
Add ``atol`` argument to function ``is_O3``
Or at least use the maximum precision of the matrix dtype instead of the arbitrarily chosen 1e-15.

https://github.com/astropy/astropy/blob/3912916dad56920514ba648be400a5f82add041a/astropy/coordinates/matrix_utilities.py#L137-L163

### Candidate patch
```diff
diff --git a/astropy/coordinates/matrix_utilities.py b/astropy/coordinates/matrix_utilities.py
index d7f1ae181..c591818cd 100644
--- a/astropy/coordinates/matrix_utilities.py
+++ b/astropy/coordinates/matrix_utilities.py
@@ -136,7 +136,7 @@ def angle_axis(matrix):
     return Angle(angle, u.radian), -axis / r
 
 
-def is_O3(matrix):
+def is_O3(matrix, atol=None):
     """Check whether a matrix is in the length-preserving group O(3).
 
     Parameters
@@ -144,6 +144,9 @@ def is_O3(matrix):
     matrix : (..., N, N) array-like
         Must have attribute ``.shape`` and method ``.swapaxes()`` and not error
         when using `~numpy.isclose`.
+    atol : float, optional
+        The absolute tolerance parameter passed to `~numpy.isclose`. If not provided,
+        the maximum precision of the matrix dtype is used.
 
     Returns
     -------
@@ -157,10 +160,14 @@ def is_O3(matrix):
     orientations. Rotations and reflections are in this group.
     For more information, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthogonal_group
     """
+    # Determine the absolute tolerance if not provided
+    if atol is None:
+        atol = np.finfo(matrix.dtype).eps
+
     # matrix is in O(3) (rotations, proper and improper).
     I = np.identity(matrix.shape[-1])
     is_o3 = np.all(
-        np.isclose(matrix @ matrix.swapaxes(-2, -1), I, atol=1e-15), axis=(-2, -1)
+        np.isclose(matrix @ matrix.swapaxes(-2, -1), I, atol=atol), axis=(-2, -1)
     )
 
     return is_o3

```

parsed.reason: The patch adds an optional `atol` argument to the `is_O3` function, allowing users to specify the absolute tolerance for comparison. If not provided, it defaults to the machine epsilon of the matrix's data type, which is a reasonable default.
